items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He played Basie and Cab Calloway and Ellington and Fletcher Henderson.

ctx.x: And yeah, it’s an interesting ride. The whole thing that got me into this, along with the music, because I’m not old enough to have been there when it was really happening. I might have been on the planet in the 1950s, but I wasn’t making any clubs. But I was a fan of this music, I still am a fan of the music. I got lucky and took some guitar lessons as a very young kid and my instructors were jazz aficionados, jazz players. So my father played classical music around the house. items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Cab Calloway’s daughter is teaching a cabaret class?

ctx.x: Well when I went up there I was going to stay for a year and a year started to go by and I liked living up there. I left one year and went to work in Washington State in construction. I got to sit in a little bit in a couple of places in Olympia and Seattle. I went back to Alaska. I went to Arizona for a season and worked on a road job. Went back to Alaska. Came back to the East Coast for about eight or nine months, went back to Alaska. There was something about it. I mean there’s two things that’ll happen to you…

performing headliners, one was Sarah Vaughan and one was Steve Allen. Yeah. I said wow. And it was a two week festival. And it wasn’t just performances. It was workshops that you could attend. And these workshops were from square dancing to photography to charcoal drawing to classical violin, singing, dancing, you name it. Arts festival. And they had to two week cabaret class. Not my thing but the instructor was a woman by the name of Chris Calloway. Cab’s daughter. Well that was enough for me to sign up. Cab…

people who really could play, as opposed to people who couldn’t play that good. That’s who I was usually playing with. And it felt good. And I thought you know I’m getting kind of tired of bouncing around on a piece of equipment, maybe I’ll go back to the East Coast. I’ll go to New York City and I’ll see if I can make a little noise.
